{{c|''Being gone to the place that Iudas the Traitor did knovv, 4 he offereth him self to the band of his enemies, showeth his Diuine might in ouerthrovving them al vvith a word, and in sauing his Apostles from them also vvith a vvord: 10 rebuketh Peter that vvould defend him from them: 12 and so being apprehended, is brought bound to Annas and Caiphas, where he is striken by a seruant, and thrise denied of Peter. 28 Againe in the morning he is by them brought to Pilate. 29 Who demaunding their accusation, whereas they would oppresse him vvith their authoritie, 33 and examining the point of his kingdom, pronounceth him innocent: yet they crie rather to haue a theeues life saued.''}} {{dropinitial|W|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial W, foliage.png|imgsize=105px|fl={{verse|chapter=18|verse=1}}}}HEN {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 36. Mr. 14, 32. Lu. 22, 39.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ THVRSDAY night. The PASSION according to S. John in these two Chapters, is the Gospel at Mass vpon Good Friday. So the PASSION is read in Holy Weeke foure times, according to the foure Evangelists, as S. Augustine appointed also in his Church at ''Hippo. Ser. 144. de tempore.''}}∷ {{sc|Iesvs}} had said these things, he went forth vvith his disciples beyond the Torrent-Cedron, vvhere vvas a garden, into the vvhich he entred and his Disciples. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=2}}† And Iudas also, that betraied him, knevv the place: because {{sc|Iesvs}} had often resorted thither together vvith his Disciples. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=3}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 47. Mr. 14, 43. Luc. 22, 47.''}}* Iudas therfore hauing receiued the band of men, and of the cheefe Priests and the Pharisees, ministers, commeth thither vvith lanternes and torches and vveapons. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=4}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore knovving al things that should come vpon him, vvent forth, and said to them, VVhom seeke ye? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=5}}† they ansvvered him, {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth. {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to them, I am he. And Iudas also that betraied him, stoode vvith them. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=6}}† As sone therfore as he said to them, I am he: they vvent backvvard, and fel to the ground. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=7}}† Againe therfore he asked them, VVhom seeke ye? And they said, {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=8}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, I haue told you, that I am he. if therfore you seeke me, let these goe their vvaies. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=9}}† That the vvord might be fulfilled vvhich he said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 17, 12.''}}* That of them vvhom thou hast giuen me, I haue not lost any. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=10}}† Simon Peter therfore hauing a svvord, drevve it out: and smote the seruant of the high priest: & cut of his right eare. And the name of the seruant vvas Malchus. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=11}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore said to Peter, Put vp thy svvord into the scabbard. The chalice vvhich my father hath giuen me, shal not I drinke it? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=12}}† The band therfore and the Tribune & the ministers of the Ievves apprehended {{sc|Iesvs}}, and bound him: {{verse|chapter=18|verse=13}}† and they brought him to Annas first, for he vvas father in lavv to Caiphas, vvho vvas the high priest of that yere. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=14}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 11, 49.''}}* Caiphas vvas he that had giuen the counsel to the Ievves, That it is expedient that one man die for the people.

{{verse|chapter=18|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 58. Mr. 14, 54. Lu. 22, 54.''}}* And Simon Peter folovved {{sc|Iesvs}}, and an other disciple. And that Disciple vvas knovven to the high priest, and<noinclude>{{rh|||vvent}}</noinclude>
